title: Coming Down
logline: On the last morning of a silent retreat, a room full of strangers who have not spoken in days says its first ordinary words, packs up, and starts down the hill together, back toward a city none of them have seen in a week.
human_question: What does it take to come back into a crowded world after time spent putting it down?

premise.story: The final day of a lay meditation retreat: the end of silence, packing, goodbyes, and the journey back down from the hills. Chathura travels with departing retreatants as far as the city.
premise.place: A hill-country lay retreat centre, not the remote forest hermitage of Episode 1, and the road and city beyond it.
premise.experience: The strange re-entry into ordinary noise and movement after days of quiet, ending in the exact crowded urban image the whole chronology has been moving toward.

concept_links.why: This is the largest map this group works with, purity of conduct through to the knowledge of the paths, and its own end point is not a private, permanent withdrawal: laypeople are told to keep taking up their precepts again and again, in ordinary life [C097-P4:L1022]. A retreat's ordinary, repeated ending, back into the world, is an honest small-scale image of that same return.

The source's account of path and fruition includes reviewing afterwards: what was gained, what is gone, what remains; the retreat's closing circle, if one exists, or simply people's own quiet reflections, can carry this without any doctrinal claim.

Across the retreat's days, different participants will have practised different ones of the forty subjects the source describes; the film does not need to itemise them, only to show the variety folding back into one shared departure.

what_camera_could_observe: The final sitting, and the moment silence formally ends
The descent by road from the hills

The film's planned closing image: the road giving way to a crowded city junction, traffic, pedestrians and overlapping sound, where Chathura is set down among the crowd, described here only as the planned ending, not as invented content
what_must_be_real: A real retreat, its real participants (with consent) and its real schedule. The film does not stage the end of silence or any participant's words.

possible_arc.turn: Silence ends; the retreat becomes an ordinary group of people again.
possible_arc.ending_open: The descent, and the planned closing image of arrival in the crowded junction shared with Episode 1 and Episode 100.

position_hint: closing candidate: a collective, communal route to the same required closing image, hands directly to the planned crowded-location event that ends the chronological development slate (released as Episode 99) and opens both Episode 1 and Episode 100.

requirements: A real lay retreat centre and a cohort willing to be filmed on their final day
A road connecting the centre to a real, busy city junction
Consent from the centre and every participant shown

suggestions.name: A hill-country lay meditation retreat centre, with the road leading toward Colombo
suggestions.why: Colombo's Fort and Pettah areas are well-known busy urban junctions suitable for the required crowded-location ending; the exact junction is undecided.
suggestions.verify: No specific retreat centre or exact junction is identified; the crowded-location choice belongs to Chathura.

risks: Overlapping visually with Episode 1's monastery material; this must stay a clearly different, lay, hill-country retreat, not a forest hermitage
Retreat centres may have strict no-filming rules during silence
Implying any participant has attained anything
drop_if: No retreat centre will permit filming even at the edges of a silent period, or participants are unwilling to be shown

connections.note: A different route to the same required closing image: a retreat's collective return, rather than an individual's final letting go.
From a single day's class matching many people to many objects, to one retreat's shared, collective ending.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
